chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim al-Karkhi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who owned a large village and had among its inhabitants non-Muslims (dhimmis), so the ruler took the jizya (poll tax) from them and gave it to them; but from one of them fifty was taken, and from some thirty, and less and more. Then the owner of the village made a settlement with the ruler for them, and then he took from them more than what he gave to the ruler. He said: 'This is haram (forbidden).'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on a landlord collecting more tax from dhimmis than he remits to the government?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the economic justice of the jizya system, ruling that if a landowner acts as an intermediary collector, retaining the surplus between the state's fixed rate and the amount collected from tenants constitutes unlawful gain (haram). This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on preventing exploitation within the tax collection hierarchy, ensuring that the 'protection money' remains a tribute to the state rather than a source of private profit for the landlord. It highlights the principle that any excess taken beyond the agreed obligation is considered unjust enrichment.
